transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… people at work got scared, I guess. I’ve been kind of… freezing up during service, and doing things wrong. Like I’ll be by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, just saying table numbers over and over instead of closing checks. They told me I should come talk to someone.
During one of these episodes, are you aware of what's happening around you and can you remember it afterward, or does it feel like a blank period you can't recall?

I’m… kind of aware, I think. It’s not totally blank. I remember standing there by the soda station with the key in my hand, and saying the table numbers, but it’s like I wasn’t putting it together right. Like I knew service was happening, but I wasn’t doing the next thing.
When one of these episodes happens, about how long does it typically last—seconds, a couple of minutes, or longer?

Longer than seconds. I don’t know exactly… maybe a few minutes? Long enough that people notice, because I’m just standing there with the key or saying the table numbers instead of doing what I’m supposed to do.
After one of these episodes ends, do you feel unusually tired, confused, or foggy for a while afterward, or do you feel back to normal right away?

I don’t know if I’d say tired exactly. More like… embarrassed and trying to catch up. People are looking at me because I was just standing there with the key or saying table numbers, and then I have to figure out what I was supposed to be doing.

During these episodes, do you notice yourself making any repetitive movements you can't control—like lip-smacking, chewing, fumbling with your clothes, or picking at objects—besides saying the table numbers?

Not really like lip-smacking or that. I don’t think I’m picking at things. It’s more… I freeze up, or I do the steps wrong. Like I’ll be standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key and just repeating table numbers instead of closing the checks. That’s what people noticed.
Do these episodes tend to happen during particularly stressful or overwhelming moments at work, or do they seem to occur randomly, even when things are calm?

It’s mostly when work gets busy, I think. Like in the middle of service, when there’s a lot going on. That’s when I’ll freeze up or do things out of order… like standing there with the cash drawer key and saying table numbers instead of closing checks. It scared people, I guess.
During or after these episodes, have you ever bitten your tongue, lost control of your bladder or bowels, or gotten injured (like falling or bruising)?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed anything like that… no one’s told me I fell or anything.
Outside of these specific episodes at work, have you noticed any ongoing problems with your memory, concentration, or getting confused about things in your day-to-day life?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I misplace things sometimes or lose track like anyone, but I haven’t noticed anything big outside of work. Nothing I can point to.
Right before one of these episodes starts, do you ever notice any warning signs—like a strange smell or taste, a feeling of déjà vu, dizziness, or a rising sensation in your stomach?
I don’t really notice anything like that beforehand. It just sort of… happens, as far as I can tell. Maybe I’m already stressed, but no smells or weird taste or anything I’ve picked up on.
Have you ever had an episode like this outside of work, during other stressful situations, or has it only happened while you're on shift?

It’s mostly been at work, on shift. Like… during service I’ll just freeze up or do things in the wrong order. People got scared because I was standing by the soda station with the cash drawer key, repeating table numbers instead of closing checks. I don’t really remember it happening other places like that.

Have you experienced other periods in your life that were just as stressful or high-pressure as busy work shifts—like personal crises or deadlines—and if so, did anything like these freezing episodes happen then too?

I guess I’ve had stressful stuff before, yeah, but not really like this. I don’t remember freezing that way except at work. That’s what scared people—the middle of service, I’d just stop or do things out of order, like standing by the soda station with the cash drawer key and saying table numbers instead of closing checks.

During one of these episodes, if a coworker calls your name, touches your arm, or tries to get your attention, does that ever snap you out of it or change what you're doing, or do you stay completely unresponsive to them until it passes on its own?

I don’t really know. People say they tried to get my attention, but I guess I didn’t change much right away. I was just kind of stuck… or doing the wrong thing, like holding the drawer key by the soda station and saying table numbers instead of finishing checks. Then after a bit I’d sort of come back.
Have you ever had one of these episodes happen while you were asleep, just waking up, or during a completely calm, low-stress moment unrelated to work?

Not that I know of. It’s been… the thing everyone noticed was at work, during service. I’d freeze or do things all wrong, like being by the soda station with the cash drawer key and saying table numbers instead of closing checks. I don’t think it happened waking up or when everything was calm.
Has one of these episodes ever happened when you were completely alone, with no one else around to notice?

I don’t think so. I mean… the times people really noticed were at work, in the middle of service. I’d just freeze or do things out of order, like ending up by the soda station with the cash drawer key, saying table numbers instead of closing checks. If I was alone, I don’t know that I’d even notice it the same way.
Is there any family history of epilepsy or seizure disorders, or have you ever had a head injury, high fever seizures as a child, or other neurological problems?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think there’s anything like that in my family, at least not that I’ve been told. And I don’t remember having seizures or a head injury or anything… not that I know of.
Around the time these episodes started, was there any particular emotional stress, conflict, or difficult life event happening for you—either at work or in your personal life?

I guess… yeah, it kind of started after they asked me to take on evening shift lead stuff. It’s been building since then, maybe about a year and a couple months. I don’t know if I’d call it one event, but that’s when things started feeling different.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes recurrent episodes of altered awareness and disorganized, automatic-like behavior (freezing, repeating table numbers, holding the cash drawer key) occurring specifically during high-stress work periods. Episodes last minutes, are partially remembered, and are not associated with classic epileptic features (no aura, no tongue biting, no incontinence, no postictal confusion, no occurrence during sleep or rest). The episodes are tightly linked to psychosocial stress (recent promotion to shift lead) and functional impairment at work, consistent with a dissociative (conversion) process rather than a neurological or primary anxiety disorder. Lack of a clear subtype (e.g., dissociative amnesia, trance, or motor symptoms) supports coding as unspecified dissociative disorder.
